title: The Ambiguity Sweep
takeaway: When a concept token's input embedding is replaced by a weighted mix of two country embeddings, early layers track the mixture smoothly, but from the workspace onset (around layer 38) the activation commits sharply to one country or the other. The paper reads this as the model's analogue of ignition, and the commitment is at least as sharp in the J-space component as in the full activation.
walkthrough:
The experiment behind this figure manufactures an input that sits between two meanings. A sentence such as "My sister has always wanted to visit ___" normally ends in a country name. At that position the model instead receives a mixed input embedding, $(1-\alpha)\,e_B + \alpha\,e_A$, where $e_A$ and $e_B$ are the input embeddings of two single-token country names. At $\alpha = 0$ the input is purely country $B$. At $\alpha = 1$ it is purely country $A$. In between it is neither. This construction is the [[embedding-mixture-experiment]]. Sixteen country pairs crossed with forty carrier sentences give the trials; for each trial, $\alpha$ sweeps from 0 to 1 while the [[residual-stream]] at the mixed position is recorded at every layer.

Panel A prints example carrier sentences with the mixed embedding in place of the country token.

Panel B reads the result without any lens. For each trial and layer, the activation is placed along the straight line connecting that trial's pure-$B$ activation to its pure-$A$ activation at the same position and layer. Its position on that line is the [[projection-share]], which by construction is 0 at one end of the sweep and 1 at the other. The panel plots this share against $\alpha$, aligned to each trial's own switching threshold, and against layer. Layers are indexed 0 to 100 under the paper's [[layer-percentage-indexing]], so a layer number reads as a percentage of depth. In early layers the share varies smoothly with $\alpha$, roughly proportional to the input mixture. From around layer 38 — the workspace onset located by the preceding boundary analyses of the [[workspace-layers]] — the share instead sits near one endpoint or the other, flipping sharply at a threshold value of $\alpha$.

Panel C brings in the [[jacobian-lens]]. The left half shows, at each layer and $\alpha$, the [[j-lens-readout]] rank of whichever country ranks higher. In very early layers neither country ranks highly. Unambiguous inputs enter the readout after a few layers; maximally ambiguous ones only by layer 38. The right half repeats the panel-B measurement restricted to the activation's component along the two countries' J-lens directions, and it resembles panel B.

The paper reads the sharp late commitment as the analogue of [[ignition]] in [[global-workspace-theory]]. Appendix 10.15 adds that at maximal ambiguity, mid- and late-layer trials cluster near 0 or 1 rather than 0.5 ([[bimodal-commitment]]), and that the [[j-space]] component's transition sharpens somewhat earlier than the rest of the activation ([[transition-width]]).

terms.definition: The interpolation coefficient, swept from 0 to 1. It sets the weight of concept $A$'s embedding in the mixture; $1-\alpha$ is the weight of concept $B$'s.
The input embeddings of the two single-token country names in a pair. These are the vectors mixed to form the ambiguous input.
The mixed embedding substituted for the concept token inside an ordinary sentence — the paper's construction of an artificially ambiguous input.
Example carrier sentences with the mixed embedding standing in for the country token, showing what the model actually receives.
A lens-free readout: the activation's position along the line from the trial's pure-$B$ activation to its pure-$A$ activation, plotted against $\alpha$ (aligned to each trial's threshold) and layer.

The J-lens view. Left: the lens rank of whichever of the two countries ranks higher, by layer and $\alpha$. Right: the panel-B projection share restricted to the activation's component along the two countries' J-lens directions.

Where an activation sits along the line connecting the same trial's pure-$B$ and pure-$A$ activations at the same position and layer. By construction it is exactly 0 at one end of the sweep and exactly 1 at the other.

The activations recorded on the same trial when the input embedding is entirely one country's ($\alpha = 0$) or entirely the other's ($\alpha = 1$). They anchor the two ends of the projection-share line.
The vertical axis of panels B and C: depth in the model, reported as a percentage 0 to 100 under the paper's convention of reindexing 25 evenly spaced residual-stream layers.

The per-trial value of $\alpha$ at which the late-layer response flips from one country to the other. Panel B's $\alpha$ axis is centered on each trial's own threshold so the switch aligns across trials.
An ordinary sentence, such as "My sister has always wanted to visit ___", that provides a natural context for the mixed embedding. Forty are used.

The rank of a country's token in the J-lens readout — the softmax over vocabulary scores obtained by projecting the activation through the layer's Jacobian and the unembedding. A low rank means the concept is prominent in the readout.
The per-token vectors of the Jacobian lens; panel C right projects the activation onto the two countries' vectors before recomputing the projection share.

The layer, around 38, at which the paper's earlier boundary metrics say the J-space begins acting as a workspace. This figure tests whether that layer coincides with ignition-like commitment, and finds that it does.

In global workspace theory, the late, all-or-none amplification of one interpretation of an ambiguous input, with bimodal outcomes at threshold. The sharp switching in this figure is the paper's proposed analogue.
The sixteen pairs of single-token country names whose embeddings are interpolated. Country names give clean single-token concepts that fit the same sentence frames interchangeably.

numbers.meaning: The range of the interpolation coefficient $\alpha$. At 0 the input embedding is purely country $B$; at 1 it is purely country $A$; each trial sweeps the whole range.
Country-name pairs used. Each pair supplies the two embeddings $e_A$ and $e_B$ being interpolated.
Carrier sentences per pair. Crossing sentences with pairs gives the trials over which panels B and C aggregate.

The layer (as a percentage of depth) from which the projection share stops varying smoothly and instead sits near 0 or 1, flipping sharply at a threshold. It matches the workspace onset located independently by the paper's boundary metrics, which is the point of the figure.
The endpoints of the projection share, exact by construction: the pure-$B$ and pure-$A$ activations define the line the share is measured along, so the sweep's ends land on them.
The rank window used in panel C: a country counts as present in the readout when it appears in the J-lens top 25, and the right half of panel C is computed within the layers where this holds.

The projection share a trial would show if the activation faithfully reflected a balanced input mixture. Appendix 10.15 reports that at maximal ambiguity, mid- and late-layer trials instead cluster near 0 and 1 — per-trial commitment, not faithful ambiguity — and most sharply so in the J-space component.
